text: Mexico arrests FBI most-wanted drug lord Chapo Isidro. Mexican security forces have arrested notorious drug cartel leader Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, popularly known as Chapo Isidro, during a military operation in Guasave, Sinaloa State. The arrest took place on Friday, November 20, following an operation involving Mexican Army and National Guard special forces, with support from United States intelligence agencies, the New York Post reported on Saturday. Meza Flores, “described by American authorities as a major drug trafficker, was reportedly arrested alongside two alleged associates identified as Germán N, also known as Serafín, and José N, who was said to be responsible for the organisation’s financial operations.” The three suspects were subsequently flown to Mexico City. The operation reportedly triggered violent confrontations between security forces and suspected cartel members, resulting in gunfire, road blockades and the burning of vehicles in parts of Sinaloa. According to the New York Post, “gunshots also disrupted a baseball match in Guasave, forcing players and spectators to flee. The match was subsequently abandoned.” Meza Flores’ arrest is considered a major development in the fight against drug trafficking, particularly because he was among the Federal Bureau of Investigation’s 10 most-wanted fugitives. On February 4, 2025, the FBI added him to its Ten Most Wanted Fugitives list, accusing him of leading the Meza-Flores cartel, an organisation allegedly involved in trafficking fentanyl, cocaine, heroin, methamphetamine and marijuana into the United States. The US government had also announced a reward of up to \`$5m for information leading to his arrest and conviction. In announcing his addition to the list, then FBI Acting Director, Brian Driscoll, accused the cartel leader of spending about 20 years trafficking illegal drugs into the United States. Meza Flores was also accused by American authorities of involvement in kidnapping, extortion, torture and murder. According to the FBI, he was first indicted on May 2, 2012, in the United States District Court for the District of Columbia. A superseding indictment returned on November 26, 2019, charged him with drug-trafficking offences and possession of firearms. The FBI said the indictment alleged that he conspired to manufacture and distribute cocaine, heroin, methamphetamine and marijuana in the United States between 2005 and 2019. The New York Post reported that “Meza Flores faces drug-trafficking and firearms-related allegations, as well as an extradition request from the United States.” His organisation, also known as the Meza-Flores cartel, has been linked to the wider Sinaloa criminal network and has operated in the northern Mexican state. The arrest comes amid renewed security operations against criminal organisations in Sinaloa, where suspected cartel members have repeatedly clashed with security forces. Authorities reportedly deployed additional security personnel following the violence that erupted during Friday’s operation, while efforts were made to reopen affected roads and restore normal activities in the area. According to PUNCH’s report, a fellow Mexican, Joaquín ‘El Chapo’ Guzmán was arrested on February 22, 2014, in Mazatlán, Sinaloa, Mexico. He was subsequently rearrested on January 8, 2016, after escaping from prison in July 2015. He was extradited to the United States on January 19, 2017. Fallen drug lord “El Chapo” was locked up in 2019 at the ADX federal maximum security prison in the US state of Colorado, where he will spend the rest of his days.
